Share on X Telegram Agianpe Onyema, Secretariat Coordinator of the Nigerian Civil Society Situation Room, has described the voter accreditation process during the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) mock election as largely smooth, despite a minor technological glitch.
Speaking to RBN in Abuja on Saturday, Onyema said civil society observers arrived at the polling unit around 8am, with voters beginning to turn up shortly after 8:30am.
She said two voters were successfully accredited and cast their ballots before leaving, adding that some voters confirmed receiving text messages informing them that their polling units had been selected for the mock election.
According to her, the exercise is designed to identify potential technological lapses in INEC’s electoral systems ahead of the main election, giving the commission time to address any challenges.
Onyema said only one voter encountered difficulty using his phone for accreditation, but the issue was resolved after several attempts.
“Of course, the system may have one or two issues, but it’s not something that we should worry about,” she said.
She added that alternative accreditation using voters’ photographs could be deployed if the technology fails.
Onyema, however, said observers had yet to witness any issues relating to the uploading of election results, noting that the process would only take place after voting ends.
She andded that observers would be able to assess the result-uploading process from about 2:30pm, when voting is expected to have concluded.
